laws.rule: In Greece, it's illegal to: not carry a photo ID, such as a clear photocopy of your passport carry weapons of any type (including pocketknives and pepper spray) smoke in indoor public places. The penalty is a fine of up to 500 euros. engage in sexual conduct with a person aged under 15 breach customs rules about the export of Greek antiquities It's also illegal to take photos of: military installations military personnel places with signs banning photography
laws.heading: Other laws

laws.rule: Codeine and other prescription opiates can only be issued with a prescription from an accredited Greek medical professional. By email: [see source] / [see source]
laws.heading: Medications

laws.rule: A valid Australian driver licence is officially recognised in Greece, though digital licences may not be accepted. If you plan on driving, you may not need an International Driving Permit. Contact the Greek Embassy or Consulate for more information on your licence type. Your licence must be valid for the type of vehicle you'll drive, including quad bikes, motorbikes, mopeds, motor scooters and other similar vehicles. Check your insurance covers vehicle hire. You could face a large fine if you do
laws.heading: Driving permit

laws.rule: The HCAA says flights over ports, hospitals, archaeological sites and military or government sites need prior HCAA approval. Yellow and magenta zones on the DAGR map need an authorisation request first.

Anyone entering or leaving the European Union with cash worth EUR 10,000 or more (about A$15,900 at the RBA rate of 30 October 2026, A$1 = EUR 0.6293) must declare it to customs. Cash here means banknotes and coins, bearer cheques and similar instruments, gold and other commodities used as stores of value, and prepaid cards. Each member state sets its own penalty for not declaring; the EU regulation says penalties must be effective, proportionate and dissuasive.
laws.heading: Cash declaration (EU Regulation 2018/1672)

laws.rule: Arriving from outside the EU, the EU duty-free allowance is 4 litres of still wine and 16 litres of beer, plus one of: 1 litre of spirits over 22% alcohol, or 2 litres of fortified or sparkling wine. The EU page tells travellers to check the destination country's customs for the latest limits.
laws.heading: Duty-free alcohol from outside the EU

laws.rule: Arriving from outside the EU, the EU allowance is 200 cigarettes, 100 cigarillos, 50 cigars or 250 g of tobacco. The EU page says a lower limit (40 cigarettes, 20 cigarillos, 10 cigars or 50 g of tobacco) applies to land and sea travellers in some EU countries; check this country's customs. You can mix product types but the total must stay within the limit.
laws.heading: Duty-free tobacco from outside the EU

laws.rule: Travelling into the EU from a non-EU country, you are not allowed to bring any meat or dairy products. Limited amounts of fruit and vegetables, eggs, egg products, honey and some fish are allowed. Exceptions: up to 10 kg per person from the Faroe Islands or Greenland, and up to 2 kg of powdered infant milk, infant food or special medical foods (unopened, shelf-stable, proprietary brand), or health-related pet food for an accompanying pet. Undeclared products are confiscated and destroyed, and a fine or prosecution is possible.
laws.heading: Meat and dairy from outside the EU

laws.rule: Under Article 75 of the Schengen Convention, a traveller carrying narcotic drugs or psychotropic substances for their own medical treatment must be able to produce, at a check, a certificate issued or authenticated by a competent authority of their state of residence. The certificate form covers the substance, quantity and length of the journey. How a resident of Australia obtains one is not checked in this entry; ask this country's embassy or health authority before travel.
laws.heading: Schengen certificate for narcotic or psychotropic medicines (Article 75)

visa-preparation.fastest_entry: Visa-free short stays (90 days or less) as part of the Schengen area, in some cases.
visa-preparation.before_departure: Nothing to lodge before travel today: EES registration happens at the border. ETIAS hadn't started on 2026-11-01.
steps: Greece is in the Schengen area: short stays of 90 days or less can be visa-free in some cases; other purposes or longer stays need a visa before travel.
At the first Schengen border, give fingerprints and a photo for the Entry/Exit System (EES). It's free; nothing is needed before arrival, and sites charging for it are fraudulent.
Carry your passport when crossing borders, including inside Schengen (temporary internal checks are in place in places).
Get an entry stamp at the first Schengen entry.

drone-pilot-pathway.summary: EU baseline (EASA): register once as an operator in the state of residence or establishment, recognised across EASA states; Specific-category work in another state needs cross-border acceptance by that state's authority. National register, zone map and visitor rules checked 6 Nov 2026 (see items); footage routes not yet checked.

items.text: Not yet checked: whether the national aviation authority publishes a list of authorised operators.

EU rules (Regulations 2019/947 and 2019/945): operators register in the EASA state where they reside or are established; Specific-category operations need an operational authorisation or a standard-scenario declaration.

An operator registered in another EASA state may fly here; for Specific-category work it first gets the authorisation or STS declaration at home, then the destination authority must confirm the cross-border operation before flying. Rules for operators from outside EASA states: not yet checked.
Not yet checked: national tourism board or film commission media libraries.

The HCAA (Hellenic Civil Aviation Authority) FAQ says a non-EU resident flying in the Open category registers with the authority of the first EU country they plan to fly in; the number goes on every drone. Its own rules also describe a registration route for operators flying beyond 50 m from the pilot.

The HCAA has a visitor authorisation form (2020-era) for people without a Greek tax number, asking for a pilot certificate and insurance certificate, with conditions such as a 400 ft height limit, daylight only and visual line of sight. Check it is still current.

The official map is DAGR (Drone Aware Greece). It marks yellow and magenta zones that need an HCAA authorisation request first (the HCAA guidance says at least 5 working days ahead), and flights over ports, hospitals, archaeological sites and military or government sites need prior HCAA approval. The map can be viewed without logging in.

The GNTO Image Bank (part of the Visit Greece media kit) offers downloadable high-resolution photographs; the page describes images only, with no video or aerial holdings mentioned, and no registration step was seen. GNTO is the copyright holder. Images may be downloaded, reproduced or published if GNTO and the photographer are credited and the use promotes Greece as a tourist destination; commercial use of the material is stated to be strictly forbidden.

ancient-sites-and-mysteries.summary: 4 site(s): Pavlopetri; Delphi; Knossos; Necromanteion of Acheron. Facts from official sources; lore labelled as claims.

sites.name: Pavlopetri
sites.what: Submerged settlement opposite Elafonisos, declared an underwater archaeological site in 1976 (FEK 1431/B/1976); buildings over 9,000 m2 mapped by the Ephorate of Underwater Antiquities.

underwater.diving: Not found among the Ephorate's accessible underwater archaeological sites in this check; confirm in writing before diving
underwater.guide_or_permit: At accessible sites, divers must go with a licensed guide (Law 3409/2005); underwater photography and filming at antiquities need Ephorate permission
underwater.unesco_2001: Greece is not a party (absent from the UN treaty status list)
underwater.penalties: Violations penalised under Laws 3028/2002 and 4688/2020; touching finds is prohibited at accessible sites

lore.text: Popular theories claim Pavlopetri is a source of the Atlantis legend.
lore.label: popular lore, not an official source
